fact: An OTR notice says customs declarations (DDU) are entered in SYDONIA, where a blocking field now requires the certificate of origin to be uploaded for preferential-tariff codes.
The Togolese Revenue Office notice requires Togo-to-Mali transit operations via Burkina Faso to be generated in SYDONIA World.

Customs directors general of the Sahel Confederation (AES) states and Togo reviewed in Lome the interconnection of their customs IT systems, under instruments signed at Niamey on 23 July 2024 that set the legal framework for it.
ECOWAS says Togo was connected to the SIGMAT goods-in-transit data exchange system for its customs administration in July 2024.
Delegation vice chair Seno Soklingi cited Togo as a country where SIGMAT has been integrated into customs operations.
The government reports that from December 2025 the revenue office's Code 26 has free-zone import manifests processed electronically through the Guichet unique du commerce exterieur (GUCE).

Togo First reports GUCE currently handles the electronic coordination of foreign-trade formalities and GUFORD the maritime and port formalities, and an order of 14 October 2026 will replace both with a single Port Community System at Lomé port, with no go-live date.

Interministerial order 011 of 14 October 2026 treats the GUCE foreign-trade single window as Togo's current principal system for goods formalities, with the GUFORD maritime single window beside it, until a Port Community System replaces both.
